sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the paper does not report a functional or surface-expression assay for the tagged construct in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: MFRP is a type II single-pass TM protein: the N-terminus (1–69) is intracellular, the TM spans 70–90, and the entire C-terminal ectodomain (91–579) is extracellular. A C-terminal tag therefore lands on the extracellular face, 489 residues from the TM boundary, well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. The paper names no specific residue; because there is exactly one extracellular C-terminus, the junction is unambiguously after residue 579 (topology_derived). Python confirms residue 579 = P and residue 578 = Q. Mouse MFRP is a close ortholog of human MFRP, so this counts as indirect evidence for the equivalent human junction. Full-length mouse MFRP (close ortholog of human MFRP) with a C-terminal 3×FLAG epitope tag cloned into a pTwist Lenti SFFV lentiviral expression vector; the construct is membrane-anchored and full-length, not a secreted ectodomain.

sources.claim: The cDNAs of mouse MFRP (full length and deletion variants) with C-terminal 3× FLAG epitope in the pTwist Lenti SFFV vector were obtained from Twist Biosciences.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports a C-terminal 3×FLAG tag on full-length mouse MFRP in a lentiviral vector — a genuine membrane-anchored tagged construct. No functional or surface-expression data are cited in the clip, so validation_level is not_measured. No internal-loop or N-terminal tag evidence exists in the ledger; no other sites are proposed. The N-terminus of MFRP (residues 1–69) is intracellular and therefore not a surface-tag candidate.
